content_voiceover: This slide addresses a distinct clinical scenario, patients who are in morphologic complete remission but still have measurable residual disease, meaning MRD of ten to the negative three or greater after at least three blocks of intensive chemotherapy. Eligibility required first or later complete remission plus that persistent or recurrent MRD. The primary endpoint was MRD complete response after just one cycle of blinatumomab at fifteen micrograms per meter squared daily for up to four cycles, and the key secondary endpoint was relapse free survival at eighteen months. Looking at the patient characteristics table, this was a heavily pretreated population of one hundred sixteen patients, sixty five percent were in their first complete remission and thirty four percent in their second, with baseline MRD levels mostly clustered between ten to the negative one and ten to the negative three. The Kaplan-Meier curve at the bottom is the clinically important part, patients treated in first CR had dramatically better relapse free survival than those treated in second or third CR, a median of twenty four point six months versus eleven months, hazard ratio two point zero nine, p equals point zero zero four. The board pearl here is that blinatumomab converts MRD positive to MRD negative status, and treating earlier, in first remission rather than waiting for a second relapse, meaningfully improves relapse free survival.
keypoints: Eligibility: CR with persistent MRD >= 10^-3 after >=3 chemo blocks
Blinatumomab 15 mcg/m2/day, up to 4 cycles, MRD-CR after cycle 1
Primary endpoint MRD-CR; secondary RFS at 18 months
1st CR: median RFS 24.6 months vs 2nd/3rd CR: 11.0 months, HR 2.09
keypoint_voiceover: For MRD positive B-ALL in remission, blinatumomab converts MRD status and buys real relapse free survival, but timing matters, treating in first complete remission gave a median of nearly twenty five months versus only eleven months when given after a second or third relapse.
